text: Masaki Tsuji (辻 真先, Tsuji Masaki; born March 23, 1932 in Nagoya) is a Japanese anime screenwriter, mystery writer, manga author, travel critic, essayist, professor, and mystery fiction novel writer.[1] He was most active in the industry from the 1960s through the 1980s and served as a scriptwriter for numerous popular anime television series produced by Mushi Production, Toei Animation, and Tokyo Movie Shinsha. Tsuji is particularly recognized for his collaborations on animated adaptations of the works of Osamu Tezuka and Go Nagai. In April 2007, he led Japan's first international anime research lab as part of Digital Hollywood University.[2] On December 4, 2007, he received a lifetime achievement award at the 11th Japan Media Arts Festival.[3] On September 24, 2008, he was awarded a Special Award at the 13th Animation Kobe for his contributions to animation writing.[1][4]
